name: Jaasia
title: One of those who had taken foreign wives
summary: Jaasia (Hebrew: Ya'asai) was an Israelite from the family of Bani who lived in the period after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of those who had married foreign women and committed to sending them away in accordance with Ezra's reforms.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among those who had taken foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Jaasia is listed among the descendants of Bani who had married foreign women in violation of God's law, after the return from exile in Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reforms against mixed marriages
keyEvents.description: Ezra led a major reform calling Israelites to separate from their foreign wives to preserve the covenant with God. Jaasia was among those affected by this reform.

keyEvents.title: The assembly of the people in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: All men of Judah and Benjamin were summoned to Jerusalem within three days to address the issue of mixed marriages. Jaasia was among those who attended.

keyEvents.title: The commitment to send away foreign wives
keyEvents.description: The people agreed to separate from their foreign wives and their children, as part of Ezra's call to repentance and obedience to God's law.
